text: Changing careers used to be unusual, but nowadays many people reassess their career path several times during their working life. Some employees resign because they feel stagnant in a job with no promotion and little job satisfaction, while others become redundant when their industry changes or shrinks. Instead of panicking, career experts suggest looking at your transferable skills, since abilities such as communication or problem-solving can often be used in a completely different field. A person who decides to retrain might take evening classes to gain new qualifications, or they might work with a mentor who has already made a similar change. Networking is also important, because many opportunities come from people you know rather than online job advertisements. Although leaving a comfort zone can be frightening, taking a risk is sometimes necessary if a job leaves someone feeling burnt out or unfulfilled. Some workers even decide to become an entrepreneur or start freelance work, which allows them to adapt their schedule and be their own boss. Of course, not every change leads to better long-term prospects, so it is wise to research a new industry carefully before committing. Nevertheless, with the right planning, a career change can lead to greater happiness and personal growth.
